To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a transposon library and a genome-scale metabolic model for Neisseria meningitis and used these resources to identify the genes and pathways essential for the pathogen's growth in vitro and in human serum.
we have developed and validated a genome-scale model of N. meningitis, and used this model to identify genes that are essential for growth under different conditions.
the genome-scale metabolic model Nmb_iTM580 can be used to identify essential genes, to predict gene essentiality and to predict gene function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genes essential for meningococcal growth and survival in different media, and the use of a genome scale metabolic network to provide novel insight into meningococcal physiology.
the development and application of a systems biology approach to the study of N. meningitis, an important human pathogen.
the application of systems biology to understand the metabolism of the pathogen and how this relates to disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have generated a powerful resource for the meningococcal research community and demonstrated its utility for the study of N. meningitis metabolism and physiology.
this study describes the application, validation and utility of a genome scale metabolic network of Nm and the generation of a transposon mutant library for this pathogen.

the Nmb_iT560 model is a valuable resource for studying meningococcal biology and that the Tn5 library and the Nm_iT560 model will be useful to other researchers working on N. meningititis and other bacteria.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a powerful resource for the study of N. meningitis metabolism and physiology.
the combination of global mutagenic and systems biology approaches can provide a more detailed understanding of the biology of N. meningitis than either approach alone.

the integration of experimental data with genome-scale models can provide new insights into the biology of a pathogen and that these data can then be used to predict and validate new biological insights.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a genome scale model can be used to interrogate global mutagenesis datasets to identify genes that are essential for metabolism under different growth conditions.
a genome scale metabolic network can be used to predict essential genes in bacteria and that these essential genes are likely to encode metabolic pathways.
a genome-scale model can be used as a tool to interpret and predict the outcome of global mutagenicity data.
